long_biography.plain_text:
Independence made Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa the first emir of the State of Bahrain in 1971, a decade after he had succeeded his father as ruler. His government established a cabinet, joined the Arab League and United Nations, and introduced a constitution followed by elections to a National Assembly.

Institution-building continued across law, finance and public services. Administrative reforms reorganised the judiciary on independent foundations, while the Bahrain Monetary Agency was created soon after independence to issue currency and regulate banking. University, airport, port and housing projects also expanded during his reign. He remained emir until his death in March 1999, when his eldest son Hamad succeeded him.
